Backend and provenance

Source: vignettes/backend-provenance.Rmd
backend-provenance.Rmd

cudagraphR keeps two different histories:

  • source provenance describes how the nearest-neighbour input was computed; and
  • current compute provenance describes graph assembly or community detection performed by cudagraphR.

These histories must not be confused. Neighbours can originate on CUDA while the current graph and community algorithms still run on the CPU.

A runnable CPU graph

The core graph constructor accepts a neighbour list, so this example needs no GPU and no optional clustering package.

library(cudagraphR)

vertex_names <- paste0("cell_", 1:6)
index <- matrix(
  c(
    2, 3,
    1, 3,
    1, 2,
    5, 6,
    4, 6,
    4, 5
  ),
  nrow = 6,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(vertex_names, c("neighbor_1", "neighbor_2"))
)
distance <- matrix(
  rep(c(1, 1.25), 6),
  nrow = 6,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = dimnames(index)
)
neighbors <- list(
  index = index,
  distance = distance,
  device = "cpu"
)

graph <- cuda_knn_graph(
  neighbors,
  weighting = "gaussian",
  symmetrize = "mutual"
)

graph
#> <cuda_graph vertices=6 edges=6 weighting=gaussian source_device=cpu compute=cpu backend=Matrix>
graph$source_device
#> [1] "cpu"
graph$compute_device
#> [1] "cpu"
cuda_provenance(graph)
#> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu>
#>           stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason fallback
#>  graph_assembly        fixed-cpu    cpu  Matrix algorithm_cpu_only    FALSE
#>  output_device
#>            cpu

graph$source_device describes the neighbour input. In contrast, cuda_provenance(graph) describes only the current graph_assembly stage: it uses the CPU and the Matrix backend. A plain list has no earlier stage-level provenance, so graph$source_provenance is NULL.

Preserve an upstream history

When cudalearnr is installed, a cuda_knn result supplies its own distance and neighbour-selection stages. cuda_knn_graph() retains those stages separately from graph assembly.

if (requireNamespace("cudalearnr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  observations <- matrix(rnorm(24 * 4), 24, 4)
  rownames(observations) <- paste0("observation_", seq_len(nrow(observations)))

  neighbors_cpu <- cudalearnr::cuda_knn(
    observations,
    k = 3,
    batch_size = 8,
    device = "cpu"
  )
  graph_from_knn <- cuda_knn_graph(neighbors_cpu)

  graph_from_knn$source_device
  graph_from_knn$source_provenance
  cuda_provenance(graph_from_knn)
}
#> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu>
#>           stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason fallback
#>  graph_assembly        fixed-cpu    cpu  Matrix algorithm_cpu_only    FALSE
#>  output_device
#>            cpu

The two provenance objects answer different questions:

  • graph_from_knn$source_provenance explains the upstream distance and neighbour-selection work;
  • cuda_provenance(graph_from_knn) explains graph assembly performed now.

Community detection remains on the CPU

Louvain and Leiden use the optional igraph package. They preserve the graph assembly record as source provenance, but their current community_detection stage is always CPU.

if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  communities <- cuda_louvain(graph)

  communities$membership
  communities$source_device
  communities$source_provenance
  cuda_provenance(communities)
}
#> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu>
#>                stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason
#>  community_detection        fixed-cpu    cpu  igraph algorithm_cpu_only
#>  fallback output_device
#>     FALSE           cpu

For a cuda_communities result:

  • source_device still identifies the original neighbour source;
  • source_provenance is the graph-assembly stage;
  • upstream_provenance retains any provenance supplied by the neighbour result; and
  • cuda_provenance(communities) reports the current CPU igraph stage.

Changing the source device does not make graph assembly, Louvain, or Leiden GPU-native.

Optional CUDA source and the hardware gate

The following block runs only when both a CUDA-enabled R torch runtime and cudalearnr are available. It requires CUDA explicitly rather than using device = "auto", then verifies that CUDA neighbour computation is followed by fixed-CPU graph assembly.

The cudaverse NVIDIA workflow sets CUDAVERSE_REQUIRE_CUDA=true. Under that gate, missing CUDA hardware or a missing integration dependency is an error, not a skipped test.

require_cuda <- identical(
  tolower(Sys.getenv("CUDAVERSE_REQUIRE_CUDA", "false")),
  "true"
)
cuda_ready <- cudatensr::cuda_available()
knn_ready <- requireNamespace("cudalearnr", quietly = TRUE)

if (require_cuda && (!cuda_ready || !knn_ready)) {
  stop(
    "The hardware gate requires CUDA and the cudalearnr integration."
  )
}

if (cuda_ready && knn_ready) {
  set.seed(2)
  cuda_input <- matrix(rnorm(32 * 4), 32, 4)
  rownames(cuda_input) <- paste0("cuda_observation_", seq_len(nrow(cuda_input)))

  neighbors_cuda <- cudalearnr::cuda_knn(
    cuda_input,
    k = 3,
    batch_size = 8,
    device = "cuda"
  )
  graph_cuda <- cuda_knn_graph(neighbors_cuda)
  graph_cuda_provenance <- cuda_provenance(graph_cuda)

  stopifnot(
    identical(graph_cuda$source_device, "cuda"),
    identical(graph_cuda$compute_device, "cpu"),
    identical(graph_cuda_provenance$stage, "graph_assembly"),
    identical(graph_cuda_provenance$device, "cpu")
  )

  graph_cuda$source_provenance
  graph_cuda_provenance

  if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
    communities_cuda_source <- cuda_louvain(graph_cuda)
    stopifnot(
      identical(communities_cuda_source$compute_device, "cpu"),
      identical(
        cuda_provenance(communities_cuda_source)$device,
        "cpu"
      )
    )
  }
}

Use device = "cuda" when CUDA execution is a requirement. Use device = "auto" only when a recorded CPU fallback is acceptable.
